# PrimeBridge 0.7.1: NVIDIA-accelerated macOS on an AMD laptop panel (no MUX)

PrimeBridge lets a hackintosh laptop without a MUX switch show the desktop on its internal screen while macOS renders on the NVIDIA GPU (NullMoth driver, Metal). The internal panel is wired only to the AMD iGPU, which has no macOS driver. PrimeBridge reuses the framebuffer the firmware (GOP) left on the iGPU and makes NullMoth's frames land in it.

PrimeBridge supports the 19 AMD iGPU PCI IDs of `docs/compatibility.md`. Two laptops have run it, both with iGPU ID `0x1681`. The first is an Acer Nitro V 15 ANV15-41 (Ryzen 5 7535HS, RTX 4050 Laptop, 1920x1080 144 Hz panel), macOS 26.7.2, NullMoth 2.6.3 and 2.8.1, PrimeBridge 0.7.0 and 0.7.1 installed by `install.sh`: direct mode with the GPU copy engine, 72 Hz forced mode. The second has a Ryzen 7 6800H and an RTX 3050, and works correctly on PrimeBridge 0.7.1. The patch builds for every NullMoth tag from 2.6.3 to 2.8.1, for macOS 15 and 26, and 2.7.x has not run on a laptop. NullMoth 2.9 is not supported yet. The other iGPU IDs have not run on a laptop either. Keep an HDMI monitor at hand for your first boots.

## What is in this repository

| Item | What it is |
|---|---|
| `install.sh`, `doctor.sh`, `uninstall.sh` | Install, check and remove PrimeBridge. All three run `primebridge.py`. |
| `primebridge.py` | Detection (macOS, Command Line Tools, NullMoth, GPUs, panel, OpenCore EFI), OpenCore `config.plist` editing, install state in `/Library/PrimeBridge`, login notification after a NullMoth update. |
| `PrimeBridge-source/` | PrimeBridge sources and `build.sh`. |
| `NVRMFB-patch/nvfbforce.patch` | The source change to NullMoth's NVRMFB (`nvrm-fb.cpp`, `nvrm_vram_abi.h`) and NVAccel (`nvrm-accel.cpp`, `nvrm_vram_abi.h`). Applies to every tag from v2.6.3 to v2.8.1, not to v2.9. |
| `NVRMFB-patch/build-nvrmfb.sh` | Builds NVRMFB and NVAccel with the patch for one NullMoth version and macOS version. |
| `NVRMFB-patch/gen_edid.py` | The forced EDID for the panel's resolution (CVT reduced blanking v2, CTA-861 HDMI block above 165 MHz). |
| `NVRMFB-patch/test_nvfbforce.py` | Static checks of the patched source and of the generated EDID, on the panel and on a set from 1366x768 to 4K. |
| `test_primebridge.py` | Checks of the installer's edits to `nvrm610.conf`. |
| `.github/workflows/build.yml` | CI: tests and builds on NullMoth 2.6.3, 2.7.2 and 2.8.1 for macOS 15 and 26 at every push, and the newest NullMoth release every Monday. |
| `install-nvrmfb.sh` | Installs NVRMFB and NVAccel if the installed NullMoth is the same version, keeps the originals, rebuilds the auxiliary kernel collection. |
| `NVRMFB-patch/NullMoth-LICENSE`, `NullMoth-NOTICE` | NullMoth's license (PolyForm Noncommercial). The patched kexts are under it: noncommercial use only. |
| `docs/` | The user documentation: install guide, troubleshooting, FAQ, compatibility, internals, development. |

## How it works

### The problem

- The internal panel is physically connected to the iGPU. macOS has no driver for it, so it cannot render there.
- NullMoth drives the NVIDIA GPU, but its accelerator (NVAccel) only runs when an NVIDIA display "head" exists, which needs a monitor plugged into the NVIDIA card.
- The firmware's GOP already lit the panel and left the iGPU scanning out a plain framebuffer in its own memory (1920x1080, 32 bpp, BGRX on the test machine). Anything written there appears on the panel.

### The data path

1. With `nvfbforce=1`, NVRMFB reports the first HDMI connector of the NVIDIA GPU as connected when nothing is plugged in, with an EDID named "PrimeBridge" that `install.sh` makes for the panel (1920x1080 at 72 Hz, 160.85 MHz on the test machine). NVIDIA head 0 exists, WindowServer composites on the NVIDIA GPU with Metal, and NVAccel runs. DisplayPort cannot be faked this way because DP needs a real sink to train the link; HDMI does not.
2. For every frame, WindowServer's swap goes through `NVDisplayPipe::performTransaction` (in NullMoth's `nvrm-accel.cpp`). With zero-copy flips off (`debug.nvaccel_iop_flip=0`, which PrimeBridge enforces), stock NVAccel pages the frame out of VRAM, then copies it with the CPU into the scanout address NVRMFB gives it (`fKva`).
3. PrimeBridge finds `NVRMNVDAFramebuffer` and calls `nvScanoutRedirect`, which the patch adds to NVRMFB. From then on `nvScanoutInfo` hands NVAccel PrimeBridge's buffer instead of NVRMFB's own.
4. PrimeBridge starts in staging mode. The scanout points to a cached RAM buffer the size of NVRMFB's whole scanout allocation (`fMemBytes`, which the patched NVRMFB reports), so a later, larger mode still fits. A 60 Hz timer (20 Hz when idle) compares it row by row with a shadow copy, only after NVAccel's frame counter (`debug.nvaccel_iop_ok`) has moved, and writes changed rows to the GOP framebuffer.
5. On the first timer tick without a new frame, a few seconds after the first frame reaches the panel, PrimeBridge probes the iGPU.
   - On ID `0x1681` (680M / 660M) it maps the register BAR (BAR5). The other IDs have no register map: they log `no register map here, BAR0 write benchmark only` and time only the two BAR0 mappings below.
   - It reads `GCMC_VM_FB_OFFSET` to find the iGPU's VRAM in system RAM (`0x440000000` on the test machine, 512 MB). Linux amdgpu accesses VRAM this way on every x86 APU.
   - It writes 32 pixels through BAR0, reads them back from that RAM (after `clflush`, retrying for up to 10 ms), puts the old values back and logs `MATCH`. This works on a black screen too.
   - It times rewriting 64 identical rows (invisible) through three mappings: BAR0 as mapped at boot, BAR0 write-combined, and VRAM write-combined. It keeps the fastest.
   - If writes are fast (under 3 µs per row), the NVIDIA mode has exactly the panel's width, height and pitch, and NVRMFB's allocation fits in the panel's mapping, it points the scanout straight at the panel's framebuffer. When that framebuffer is the iGPU's VRAM in system RAM, which only ID `0x1681` can find, it also hands NVRMFB its physical address, and the patched NVAccel has the NVIDIA copy engine write each frame there by DMA, with no CPU copy. Frames whose newest pixels are not in VRAM still go through the CPU. The staging copy and the row diff drop out, and the PrimeBridge timer drops to 4 Hz to watch the geometry. The log says `direct` and `PrimeMode` becomes `direct-copy-engine` (`direct-kva` when the panel's buffer is in BAR0, where NVAccel keeps copying with the CPU).
6. Every 64 timer ticks (every tick in direct mode) PrimeBridge re-reads the NVIDIA scanout geometry. On a change (resolution switch) it asks NVRMFB to take its own buffer back and falls back to staging, then goes direct again when the geometry matches.
7. On ID `0x1681`, PrimeBridge also reads the OTG frame counter and logs the panel's real refresh rate on every `rate-hint` line.

### Why the "Fix PAT" OpenCore patch must be off

macOS maps write-combined (WC) memory through PAT entry PA6. AMD Vanilla's `_mtrr_update_action | Fix PAT` patches (Algrey's is enabled by default) replace macOS's PAT with `0x0007010600070106`, where PA6 is UC- (uncached). Every WC mapping in macOS then becomes uncached: PrimeBridge's writes, but also CPU access to NVIDIA VRAM.

On the test machine, measured per 7680-byte row:

| | Fix PAT on | Fix PAT off |
|---|---|---|
| BAR0 | 39.7 µs | 2.0 µs |
| iGPU VRAM, write-combined | 75.4 µs | 1.4 µs (about 5.7 GB/s) |
| Result | staging mode, `kernel_task` 75 % in video | direct mode, `kernel_task` 2.5 % |

AMD Vanilla's README says the patch does not improve performance and that some systems run better without it. Test without it on a USB stick first.

## Requirements

- A laptop whose internal panel is wired only to an AMD iGPU that macOS has no driver for: Radeon 680M / 660M (`1002:1681`, the only one tested), 780M / 760M / 740M (`15bf`, `15c8`, `1900`, `1901`), 890M / 880M (`150e`), 860M / 840M / 820M (`1114`, `1902`), 8060S / 8050S (`1586`) or 610M (`164e`, `13c0`, `1506`). Vega iGPUs are not matched, since NootedRed drives them. Intel iGPUs are not matched yet.
- An NVIDIA GPU that NullMoth drives, with NullMoth 2.6.3 to 2.8.1 already working: a monitor plugged into the NVIDIA GPU shows an accelerated desktop.
- An HDMI port wired to the NVIDIA GPU, with nothing plugged into it at boot. That is the case on most gaming laptops: a monitor on that port shows NullMoth's desktop. A laptop without one cannot use PrimeBridge yet.
- OpenCore, with `Misc > Security > Vault` set to `Optional`.
- macOS 15 or 26, already booting normally (USB ports mapped and so on).
- The Xcode Command Line Tools (`xcode-select --install`) and internet access for the first build, which downloads about 170 MB (NullMoth's source and NVIDIA's open-gpu-kernel-modules headers).
- A 32 bpp firmware boot framebuffer inside the iGPU's BAR0. PrimeBridge checks this and refuses otherwise.

## Installation

```bash
git clone https://github.com/myvoow/PrimeBridge.git
cd PrimeBridge
./install.sh
```

`install.sh` runs as your user and asks for your password before it changes anything. It:

1. Checks the Mac: macOS version, Command Line Tools, NullMoth version and that it runs, the NVIDIA GPU and the iGPU, the panel resolution and refresh rate, and OpenCore's EFI partition (from the boot path OpenCore records in NVRAM). `./install.sh --dry-run` shows what it finds and stops there.
2. Builds NullMoth's NVRMFB and NVAccel for the installed NullMoth version and macOS version, with the patch and a forced EDID made for the panel, then builds PrimeBridge. When it has the original kexts, it also checks that its unpatched builds match them byte for byte. A difference only means another compiler than NullMoth's, and the build is used anyway.
3. Edits OpenCore's `config.plist`, after saving a copy in `/Library/PrimeBridge`: adds PrimeBridge to `Kernel > Add`, adds the missing boot-args (`nvfb=1 nvaccel=1 nvfbforce=1 nvcursor=0 -nvrmnoflip`, plus `gfxrst=4` with WhateverGreen), removes `-primeoff`, and turns off the Fix PAT kernel patches ([why](#why-fix-pat-must-be-off)).
4. Installs the patched NVRMFB and NVAccel, keeps NullMoth's originals in `/Library/PrimeBridge`, and rebuilds the auxiliary kernel collection.
5. Adds `NVRM_EVENT_WAIT=1` to NullMoth's own settings block in `/Library/GPUBundles/nvmtl/nvrm610.conf` (`# --- my settings, kept on update ---`), unless the file already sets that key. Metal apps then sleep until the GPU is done instead of polling it: on the first laptop their CPU time dropped by 20 to 67 %, for 2 to 10 % more latency. NullMoth keeps that block when it updates. To opt out, put `NVRM_EVENT_WAIT=0` in the block: `install.sh` leaves a value that is already there alone.

Then approve the extensions in System Settings > Privacy & Security if macOS asks, unplug any monitor from the NVIDIA GPU, restart, and run `./doctor.sh`. The direct mode starts a few seconds after the first frame reaches the panel.

When detection fails, give it what it could not find: `--panel 1920x1080`, `--panel-hz 144` or `--efi disk0s1`.

The forced HDMI mode runs at a whole divisor of the panel's refresh rate (72 Hz on a 144 Hz panel). On a first install PrimeBridge has not measured the panel yet, so the mode is 60 Hz. On ID `0x1681`, PrimeBridge measures the panel, and after the restart `./doctor.sh` says when running `./install.sh` again gives a better rate. The other iGPUs cannot measure it, so pass `--panel-hz` when the panel is not 60 Hz.

`nvfb=1 nvaccel=1` belong to NullMoth, which needs its own boot-args too (see its docs). `nvfbforce=1` creates the fake HDMI monitor. `nvcursor=0` turns off the NVIDIA hardware cursor, so macOS draws the cursor into the frame and it shows on the panel.

### After a NullMoth update

NullMoth's updater puts its own NVRMFB and NVAccel back. Until `./install.sh` runs again, PrimeBridge steps aside after 2 minutes and the panel gets macOS's basic display driver, without acceleration. A notification at login says so.

NullMoth 2.9 is not supported yet: the patch does not apply to it, and `install.sh` stops before it changes anything. Do not update NullMoth past 2.8.1 for now.

### Rollback

- `./uninstall.sh` puts NullMoth's original kexts back, removes PrimeBridge and the boot-args it added from OpenCore, turns the Fix PAT patches it disabled back on, and takes out the `NVRM_EVENT_WAIT=1` line it added. Restart afterwards. Every `config.plist` the scripts changed is saved in `/Library/PrimeBridge`.
- Black internal screen: add `-primeoff` to the boot-args to stop PrimeBridge. You can also plug a monitor into the NVIDIA GPU before booting: nothing is forced then, the monitor works as usual and the panel mirrors it. When no NVIDIA head comes up within 2 minutes, PrimeBridge steps aside by itself so macOS's basic display driver can take the panel.

## Checking that it works

`./doctor.sh` prints the mode and what to do when something is wrong. Everything PrimeBridge does is logged to `/var/log/PrimeBridge.log`, started over at boot once it passes 8 MB. `./doctor.sh --report` prints the same check, plus the system, the settings and the last 60 lines of the log, in a block ready to paste into an issue.

```bash
tail -40 /var/log/PrimeBridge.log
ioreg -rc PrimeBridge -d1 | grep -E "Version|PrimeMode"
```

Expected sequence:

```
PrimeBridge 0.7.1 starting (log=1)
FB 1920x1080 bpp 32 stride 7680 B ... phys 0x490000000 ... BAR0 0x490000000 +0x10000000
found NVRMNVDAFramebuffer 1920x1080 pitch 7680 phys 0x...
NVAccel's present path armed after about 200 ms
redirected NVRMNVDAFramebuffer scanout kva to cached staging (8323072 bytes; NVRMFB allocation 8323072, GOP mapping 8323072)
igpu probe: FB_OFFSET 0x00000440 FB_LOCATION 0x0000f400..0x0000f41f -> VRAM at phys 0x440000000, 512 MB; GOP at VRAM +0x0
igpu probe: phys 0x440000000: 32 of 32 pixels written through BAR0 read back there -> MATCH
igpu writes: PAT 0x... (PA6 WC)
igpu writes: ns per row: BAR0 2004, BAR0 write-combined 2343, VRAM write-combined 1355 -> VRAM at phys, fast
NVAccel now puts its frames straight into the panel's buffer, with the GPU copy engine (no staging copy, no diff)
rate-hint: 4 Hz (idle), work avg 0 us ..., panel 143.78 Hz, direct
```

- `PA6 not WC` and writes around 40 µs per row: the Fix PAT patch is still active.
- `no NVIDIA head after 60 s: ...` (`PrimeMode` is `no-nvidia-head`): NVRMFB did not create head 0, and the line says why, from the `nvfbforce` property NVRMFB publishes on NVRM: no HDMI port on the NVIDIA GPU (`no-hdmi`), NVKMS refused the forced display (`refused`), `nvfbforce=1` missing (`off`), or no property at all, meaning an NVRMFB that `install.sh` did not build (a NullMoth update put its own back): run `./install.sh` again. After 2 minutes PrimeBridge steps aside (`still no NVIDIA head after 2 min`).
- `PrimeMode` is `no-nvaccel-present`: the NVIDIA head exists but NVAccel never armed its present path. Check `nvaccel=1`.
- `a display is plugged into the NVIDIA GPU`: nothing was forced at boot. That monitor works as usual and the panel shows a copy of it (its top-left 1920x1080 when it is larger), in staging mode, which costs more CPU than direct mode.
- No `direct` at the end of the `rate-hint` lines: compare `NVRMFB allocation` and `GOP mapping` on the `redirected` line. If the allocation is larger, NVRMFB can switch to a mode larger than the panel's buffer, so PrimeBridge stays in staging mode to keep it from writing past that buffer.
- `NVRMFB reports a scanout allocation of 0 bytes`: this NVRMFB lacks the patch from this release (0.4.x, or NullMoth's own). PrimeBridge does not redirect and copies from NVIDIA memory instead, which is slow. Run `./install.sh` again.
- `this NVRMFB has no nvScanoutRedirect`: the NVRMFB was patched by an older release. Run `./install.sh` again.
- Useful NullMoth counters: `sysctl debug.nvaccel_iop_ok debug.nvaccel_surface_gpu_timeouts debug.nvaccel_iop_copy_skip`.

## Adapting it to another laptop

### Panel resolution

Direct mode needs the NVIDIA mode to equal the GOP framebuffer: same width, height and pitch (width x 4). `install.sh` makes the forced EDID from the panel's resolution (`NVRMFB-patch/gen_edid.py`, CVT reduced blanking v2), and the pitch matches for the usual widths. Above 165 MHz the EDID gets a CTA-861 block that declares HDMI up to 340 MHz, and a mode that would need more gets a lower divisor of the panel's rate (a 60 Hz 4K panel gets 30 Hz). Only 1920x1080 has run on a laptop so far.

### A different iGPU

The GOP framebuffer path is the same on every iGPU PrimeBridge matches. Only the optional VRAM probe and the panel refresh readout use registers, taken from the Linux amdgpu headers for Rembrandt (`yellow_carp_offset.h`, `gc_10_3_0_offset.h`, `dcn_3_1_2_offset.h`), so they run on ID `0x1681` only. The other iGPUs time BAR0 writes instead, and go direct when BAR0 write-combined is fast enough. For an AMD iGPU that is not listed, add its ID to `IOPCIPrimaryMatch` in `Info.plist`. PrimeBridge never writes to the VRAM address unless it read back exactly what it had written through BAR0.

### Another NullMoth version

PrimeBridge does not touch NVRMFB's private fields: it calls `nvScanoutRedirect` and reads `nvScanoutInfo`, both answered by the patched NVRMFB. `nvScanoutInfo` also reports the scanout allocation (`fMemBytes`) and, once the scanout is redirected to memory with a physical address, flags it and gives that address to NVAccel. NVRMFB also publishes two properties on NVRM: `nvfbforce-display`, the forced display or 0, and `nvfbforce`, what the force pass did (`forced`, `monitor`, `no-hdmi`, `refused` or `off`).

`install.sh` rebuilds NVRMFB and NVAccel for whatever NullMoth version is installed. It clones that NullMoth tag, and NVIDIA's open-gpu-kernel-modules at the release the tag is built on, into `~/Library/Caches/PrimeBridge`. The release comes from `NV_XNU_FW_DIR` in NullMoth's `kexts/NVRM/os-xnu2.cpp`. NullMoth's docs lag behind: 2.8.1's docs say 615.78.08 and its code uses 620.70.06. The same `nvfbforce.patch` applies to every tag from v2.6.3 to v2.8.1, and `install.sh` stops on a version it does not apply to, such as v2.9. GitHub Actions builds the supported tags at every push and tries the newest NullMoth release every Monday.

To build by hand:

```bash
PANEL=1920x1080 PANELHZ=144 sh NVRMFB-patch/build-nvrmfb.sh 2.8.1 [stock NVRMFB binary] [stock NVAccel binary]
```

NullMoth builds a different NVAccel for macOS 15 and 26: the script builds for the Mac it runs on, and `MACOS_MAJOR=15` or `26` picks the other one. `WORK=` and `OGKM=` point it to existing checkouts, `OGKM_TAG=` overrides the NVIDIA release, and `EXTRA_PATCH=` applies one more patch after `nvfbforce.patch`. The result is in `nullmoth-<version>/patched`, and `sudo sh install-nvrmfb.sh <NVRMFB.kext> <NVAccel.kext>` installs it.

### PrimeBridge boot-args

| Boot-arg | Effect |
|---|---|
| `-primeoff` | PrimeBridge does not load (escape hatch). |
| `-primelogoff` | No log file. |
| `primecarve=0` | Skip the write benchmark (stays on BAR0 as mapped at boot, no direct mode). |
| `primehz=N` | Staging timer rate (default 60, 24 to 240). |
| `primefmt=N` | Pixel packing in staging mode: 1 = BGRX (default), 2 = RGBX, 3 = raw. Direct mode only runs with 1. |
| `primemirror=1` | Copy each frame to a monitor plugged into the NVIDIA GPU too (staging mode only). On by itself when such a monitor was there at boot. |
| `primedirect=1` | Skip the redirect and copy from NVIDIA memory, which is slow. |
| `primetest=1/2/3`, `primecolors=1` | Test patterns on the panel during boot, for checking colors and stride. |
| `primehold=N` | Seconds a `primetest` pattern stays up during boot (default 60, up to 600). |

### Building PrimeBridge

On a Mac with the Command Line Tools (no Xcode needed):

```bash
cd PrimeBridge-source
sh build.sh
```

`build.sh` uses the SDK `xcrun --show-sdk-path` reports; set `SDK=` to another SDK path if needed. Output: `build/PrimeBridge.kext` (ad-hoc signed). No floating point in kernel code: `otool -tV build/PrimeBridge.kext/Contents/MacOS/PrimeBridge | grep -cE "cvtsi2sd|divsd"` must print 0.

## Known limits

- PrimeBridge needs an HDMI port on the NVIDIA GPU. Laptops whose NVIDIA GPU has only DisplayPort or USB-C outputs, or none, are not supported yet: NVRMFB starts a head only for a connected display, and a DP link cannot be forced without a sink.
- The forced mode runs at a divisor of the panel's rate (72 Hz on 144 Hz), so each frame stays up for the same number of refreshes. The two clocks are independent, so every few seconds one frame shows for one refresh more or less.
- NVAccel waits up to 100 ms for a composite to finish before copying (`kSurfGpuWaitMs` in `nvrm-accel.cpp`). The test machine still sees a few of these per 10 minutes (`debug.nvaccel_surface_gpu_timeouts`), which show as short freezes.
- Tearing is possible: the iGPU scans out the same buffer NVAccel writes into (no double buffering).
- Sleep and wake are untested.
- Only iGPU ID `0x1681` (680M / 660M) has run on a laptop. NullMoth's opt-in AMD and Intel test driver (NMDRM) attaches to the same iGPU and has not been tried with PrimeBridge.
- A smaller mode in System Settings shows top-left without scaling.
- The NVIDIA GPU stays powered all the time because it renders the desktop, so battery life is limited.

## For an AI assistant helping with this

Read `PrimeBridge-source/src/PrimeBridge.cpp` first: `attachNvidiaScanout()` (redirect), `probeIgpu()` and `chooseWriteMapping()` (iGPU probe, write benchmark), `tickNullMoth()` (staging copy, geometry check, switch to direct mode). `BootFramebuffer.cpp` maps the GOP framebuffer (`attach()`, `mapWriteCombined()`). The NVIDIA side is `nvfbforce.patch` (tags v2.6.3 to v2.8.1): the forced HDMI display and `nvScanoutRedirect` in `kexts/NVRMFB/fb/nvrm-fb.cpp`, and `nvAccelIopToPanel`, the copy engine path of `NVDisplayPipe::performTransaction`, in `kexts/NVRM/accel/nvrm-accel.cpp`. The installer is `primebridge.py`: `detect()` (what it checks and where it reads it), `install()` (build, OpenCore edit, kexts, state), `doctor()`, `uninstall()`. Its state lives in `/Library/PrimeBridge`: the original kexts (`<name>-<version>-orig.kext`), every `config.plist` it replaced, `nullmoth-version`, `forced-mode`, `added-boot-args` and `disabled-patches`. Diagnose with `./doctor.sh`, `/var/log/PrimeBridge.log` and `ioreg -rc PrimeBridge` before changing code.
